# nja

`njar` is an R port of the [NJA python
package](https://github.com/fwimp/NJA) for fitting graphs to images of
spatial networks.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `njar` like so:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("fwimp/njar")
```

## Python dependency - `scikit-image`

In order to provide an option for skeletonization `njar` can call the
python library `scikit-image`.

For most people this should work as-is (given `reticulate` - the package
used to call python under-the-hood - is very mature).

If you do not (or cannot) run a python environment for any reason, or if
this does not work for some reason, you can perform the skeletonization
process externally using something like [Fiji](https://fiji.sc/) and
then import this image with the following command:

``` r

library(njar)
img <- import_image("path/to/image.png", skeletonize = FALSE)
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`NJANet`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/NJANet.md) : NJA
  network class
- [`NJANode`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/NJANode.md) : NJA
  node class
- [`border_matrix()`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/border_matrix.md)
  : Add an external border to a matrix
- [`find_adj_stack()`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/find_adj_stack.md)
  : Find adjancencies by stacking shifted versions of a matrix
- [`generate_test_matrix()`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/generate_test_matrix.md)
  : Generate a random binary map
- [`load_image()`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/load_image.md)
  : Load an image into njar
- [`load_skel()`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/load_skel.md) :
  Load a pre-skeletonized image into njar
- [`map_junctions()`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/map_junctions.md)
  : Map the number of white pixels that each white pixel neighbours
- [`trace_all_paths()`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/trace_all_paths.md)
  : Trace the path between all junctions in a binary map
- [`trace_path()`](https://fwimp.github.io/njar/reference/trace_path.md)
  : Trace the path between two junctions over a binary map
